entities.summary: Claus Offe was a German political sociologist associated with the Frankfurt School who taught at universities in Germany and the United States, with a focus on political economic analysis. He found new perspectives for a wide range of topics such as analysis of social crises, the welfare state, the transformation of Eastern Europe and European integration, unconditional basic income, civil society and the common good. Offe was a founding member of the Greens and of the Hertie School. Claus Offe was a writers & intellectuals from Berlin (1940-03-16, Berlin–2025-10-01). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Claus Offe's work on political economic analysis and his ideas on unconditional basic income have influenced contemporary debates on social welfare and European integration. His contributions to the Frankfurt School have shaped the discussion on civil society and the common good.
